knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

# Load the Packages
```{r}
library(readxl)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)
library(urca)
library(vars)
```

# Import the ABS Excel File
```{r}
raw <- read_excel(
  "5206025_SFD_Summary.xlsx",
  sheet = "Data1",
  col_names = TRUE
)

dim(raw)
```

# Find Columns Using Series ID
```{r}
which(raw == "A2303111F", arr.ind = TRUE)
which(raw == "A2303139J", arr.ind = TRUE)
which(raw == "A2303187A", arr.ind = TRUE)
which(raw == "A2302956R", arr.ind = TRUE)
which(raw == "A2302984X", arr.ind = TRUE)
which(raw == "A2303012X", arr.ind = TRUE)

# Extract the data
selected <- raw[10:173, c(1, 16, 41, 66, 91, 116, 141)]

names(selected) <- c(
  "Quarter", "NSW", "VIC", "QLD", "SA", "WA", "TAS"
)

selected$Quarter <- as.Date(
  as.numeric(selected$Quarter),
  origin = "1899-12-30"
)

# Check data
head(selected$Quarter)
tail(selected$Quarter)
sum(is.na(selected))
range(selected$Quarter)
str(selected)

# Convert six SFD columns to numeric
selected <- selected |>
  mutate(
    NSW = as.numeric(NSW),
    VIC = as.numeric(VIC),
    QLD = as.numeric(QLD),
    SA = as.numeric(SA),
    WA = as.numeric(WA),
    TAS = as.numeric(TAS)
  )

str(selected)
```

# EDA/Descriptive Check
```{r}
summary(selected)

# Check for missing value
colSums(is.na(selected))
```

```{r}
# Plot the six SFD series
plot_data <- selected |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -Quarter,
    names_to = "State",
    values_to = "SFD"
  )

p <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = Quarter, y = SFD, colour = State)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    title = "State Final Demand Across Australian States",
    x = "Quarter",
    y = "State Final Demand ($ million, log scale)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggsave("sfd_levels_log.png", plot = p, width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 300)

# Cleaned CSV
write.csv(
  selected,
  "SFD_clean.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
# Create the train/test split
train <- selected |>
  filter(Quarter <= as.Date("2025-06-01"))

test <- selected |>
  filter(Quarter >= as.Date("2025-09-01"))

# Check
dim(train)
dim(test)

range(train$Quarter)
range(test$Quarter)

sum(is.na(train))
sum(is.na(test))
```
# ADF Stationarity Test
```{r}
adf_nsw <- ur.df(
  train$NSW,
  type = "trend",
  lags = 4
)

summary(adf_nsw)

adf_vic <- ur.df(train$VIC, type = "trend", lags = 4)
adf_qld <- ur.df(train$QLD, type = "trend", lags = 4)
adf_sa  <- ur.df(train$SA,  type = "trend", lags = 4)
adf_wa  <- ur.df(train$WA,  type = "trend", lags = 4)
adf_tas <- ur.df(train$TAS, type = "trend", lags = 4)

summary(adf_vic)
summary(adf_qld)
summary(adf_sa)
summary(adf_wa)
summary(adf_tas)
```
Since none of the six ADF statistics is more negative than −3.43, we fail to reject H₀ for every state. So, the overall conclusion is: All six SFD series are non-stationary in levels at the 5% significance level.


```{r}
# ADF-test the first differences
adf_nsw_d1 <- ur.df(diff(train$NSW), type = "drift", lags = 4)
adf_vic_d1 <- ur.df(diff(train$VIC), type = "drift", lags = 4)
adf_qld_d1 <- ur.df(diff(train$QLD), type = "drift", lags = 4)
adf_sa_d1  <- ur.df(diff(train$SA),  type = "drift", lags = 4)
adf_wa_d1  <- ur.df(diff(train$WA),  type = "drift", lags = 4)
adf_tas_d1 <- ur.df(diff(train$TAS), type = "drift", lags = 4)

summary(adf_nsw_d1)
summary(adf_vic_d1)
summary(adf_qld_d1)
summary(adf_sa_d1)
summary(adf_wa_d1)
summary(adf_tas_d1)
```
All six first-differenced SFD series are stationary at the 5% significance level.

# Investigate the Lag-length for the Six-state VAR system
```{r}
# Create the six-state training dataset
train_var <- train |>
  dplyr::select(NSW, VIC, QLD, SA, WA, TAS)

head(train_var)
dim(train_var)

# Lag selection
lag_selection <- VARselect(
  train_var,
  lag.max = 8,
  type = "const"
)

lag_selection$selection
lag_selection$criteria
```
Preliminary lag selection favours a short lag structure, with HQ and FPE selecting two lags. VAR(2) is therefore used as the initial specification for the cointegration analysis, subject to diagnostic checking.

# Johansen Test
```{r}
# Trace test
johansen_test <- ca.jo(
  train_var,
  type = "trace",
  ecdet = "const",
  K = 2,
  spec = "transitory"
)

summary(johansen_test)
```
The Johansen trace test suggests a cointegration rank of r = 3 at the 5% significance level. The current preliminary specification is: Six-variable VECM with cointegration rank 3 and underlying VAR lag order 2.

```{r}
# Maximum eigenvalue test
johansen_max <- ca.jo(
  train_var,
  type = "eigen",
  ecdet = "const",
  K = 2,
  spec = "transitory"
)

summary(johansen_max)
```
Maximum eigenvalue test suggests r = 1 at the 5% level. 

The Johansen trace test suggested three cointegrating relationships, whereas the maximum-eigenvalue test supported one. Given this difference, the rank selection was treated cautiously, with a rank-one VECM considered the more parsimonious specification and evaluated alongside alternative specifications.

# Sensitivity Check of the Johansen Rank Under VAR(6)
```{r}
# Trace test and maximum eigenvalue test for Var(6)
johansen_k6_trace <- ca.jo(
  train_var,
  type = "trace",
  ecdet = "const",
  K = 6,
  spec = "transitory"
)

summary(johansen_k6_trace)

johansen_k6_eigen <- ca.jo(
  train_var,
  type = "eigen",
  ecdet = "const",
  K = 6,
  spec = "transitory"
)

summary(johansen_k6_eigen)
```
Trace consistently suggests 3 cointegrating relationships, while max-eigenvalue consistently suggests 1, under both K = 2 and K = 6. Hence, the test results shows that changing the lag specification from K = 2 to K = 6 does not change the rank conclusions.
